overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a single councilor's conversation with two non-members did not reach a quorum, and the chair's limit on public participation was within his discretion.

allegations.summary: A councilor allegedly deliberated on municipal aggregation with two non-member individuals during a February 6 meeting recess, outside the posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the communication was between one Council member and two individuals not on the Council, and which did not otherwise reach a quorum of the Council, the communication did not constitute deliberation, even if an opinion was expressed.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged the council did not allow him to ask questions during the February 6 meeting public comment period.
allegations.key_passage: As it is within the chair's discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by doing so here.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
